transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just keep having these evenings where I end up buying a whole family-size takeout order, and then I'll add on chips or bakery things from the grocery store. I end up eating most of it myself before I even really seem to register how much is actually gone.
After an evening of eating like that, do you do anything to try to undo it or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up or using laxatives?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything to try and undo it. I mostly just... well, I just sit there feeling terrible and overly full afterwards, but I don't do anything to actually get rid of the food.
About how often do these episodes happen in a typical week?

Well, when I look back through my journal, there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks it happens several times. I'd say maybe... four or five times a week, usually.
During these times, do you feel like you cannot stop eating or control how much you are eating?

Yes, that is exactly what it feels like. Once I start, there is just this awful switch that flips. I can literally be thinking to myself, Taylor, put it away, but my hands just keep opening containers anyway. It really feels like I am not the one in charge anymore.

inference_history.note: Patient describes binge-eating episodes characterized by consuming unusually large quantities of food with a subjective loss of control, raising suspicion for Bulimia Nervosa, Binge-Eating Disorder (under F50.8), or Eating Disorder, Unspecified.
Ruled out F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) due to absence of compensatory behaviors like vomiting or laxative use.
